urls.title: Please send x-opencode-session header on API requests (OpenCode Go requires it from 09/05) · deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness · Discussion #5495
urls.content:
*   [Oldest](/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5495?sort=old)
*   [Newest](/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5495?sort=new)
*   [Top](/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5495?sort=top)

Measured on a shipped install (`dsh 0.1.6-alpha.2`, `opencode-go` route through the `llm-pi-ai` adapter), and on this route it is not a coverage gap — **every** request fails hard:

```
HTTP 400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"MissingSessionID","message":"Error from provider (Console Go): Request is missing x-opencode-session and cannot be routed efficiently."}}
```

Direct probes against `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` (`deepseek-v4.1-flash`, minimal non-streaming request), one header at a time:

header sent

result

_(none)_

400 `MissingSessionID`

`x-opencode-session: <uuid>`

200

`x-session-id: <uuid>`

200

`session_id: <uuid>`

200

`x-session-affinity: <uuid>`

400 `MissingSessionID`

`x-client-request-id: <uuid>`

400 `MissingSessionID`

So Go accepts `x-opencode-session` or a generic `x-session-id` / `session_id`, but not two of the three headers pi-ai's own affinity branch emits.

**Why it cannot be fixed from configuration today.** Both affinity switches are withheld: `sendSessionAffinityHeaders` and `sessionAffinityFormat` are `"withhold"` in `COMPAT_GATES` (`dsh-llm-pi-ai/lib/index.js:404,406` in the installed build), and pi-ai's branch (`@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/api/openai-completions.js:557`) only ever writes `x-session-id` (openrouter format) or `session_id` + `x-client-request-id` + `x-session-affinity`. No adapter sends `x-opencode-session`.

**Workaround that works today** (verified live — a real turn completes after the change): the session id is already plumbed into the request, it is just not used for headers (`dsh-llm-pi-ai/lib/index.js:1917` passes `sessionId: String(options.sessionId)`, `:1919` sets `headers`), so a static value on the provider profile is enough:

llm-pi-ai:
  providers:
    opencode-go:
      headers:
        x-opencode-session: "<one stable uuid per install>"

That is exactly what [@RaulLazaro](https://github.com/RaulLazaro)'s `sessionHeader` field would make per-conversation: the plumbing already exists, so the change is small — a profile string naming the header, written from `options.sessionId` on every request. One stable id per install satisfies the gateway (routing is stable, prompt caching keeps working) but cannot express per-conversation affinity, which is what your docs ask for.

Adding evidence from a **library-level** consumer of `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, which narrows where the remaining work actually is.

**The gap is adapter-specific, and the missing half is the pi-ai adapter.**

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek` (provider `deepseek-official`) already sends the header on both of its protocols:

*   `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/messages/adapter.ts:130` → `x-deepseek-harness-session-id`
*   `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/chat-completions/adapter.ts:264` → `x-deepseek-harness-session-id`

That is why a DeepSeek route pointed at `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` works today. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` sends **no session header at all**:

*   it passes the harness session id into pi-ai (`packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/adapter.ts:384`) and merges only profile + attribution headers per request (`:388`);
*   in `@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.85.1` there is no `x-opencode-session` anywhere, `sessionAffinityFormat` is only `"openai" | "openrouter"`, and `sendSessionAffinityHeaders` is `false` unless a catalog entry or compat layer turns it on — no shipped `opencode-go` entry does;
*   the header injection that does exist (`getSessionHeaders()` → `x-opencode-session` + `x-opencode-client: pi`) lives in **`pi-coding-agent`'s `provider-attribution.js`**, i.e. the CLI layer — **not** in the `@earendil-works/pi-ai` library that DSH consumes.

Upstream `earendil-works/pi#9230` was closed as resolved on the strength of the CLI-layer path. That resolution does not cover library consumers, so "send it across all adapters" is still open for `dsh-llm-pi-ai`.

**Wire evidence** (Go key, `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`, `model: deepseek-v4.1-flash`):

Request headers

Result

no session header (also with the DSH user-agent)

`400 MissingSessionID`

`x-deepseek-harness-session-id: <id>`

`200`

`x-opencode-session: <id>`

`200`

So the endpoint accepts DSH's native header — the id just never reaches the wire on this path.

**The fix looks small.** `PiAiAdapter.stream()` already has `options.sessionId` in hand at the same call that builds `headers` (`adapter.ts:388`), so the id can be sent there. Sending it only for OpenCode routes (e.g. `model.baseUrl` containing `opencode.ai`) would avoid leaking a harness session id to every third-party provider; the alternative — always sending `x-deepseek-harness-session-id`, mirroring `dsh-llm-deepseek` — is also defensible and more uniform.

Happy to test a patch if that is useful.

**Reconciling the three proposed paths: they do not have the same coverage, and one of them closes both 400s at once.**

The thread now carries three candidate fixes — [@Jay0130-a](https://github.com/Jay0130-a)'s in-tree adapter patch, [@itchenshi](https://github.com/itchenshi)'s out-of-tree plugin, and widening the dependency range. They get discussed as interchangeable, but they differ in _which_ of the two 400s they close, and that decides whether the model is actually usable afterwards. I pulled the published artifacts and checked.

### 1\. The second 400 does not exist on the catalog path

[@itchenshi](https://github.com/itchenshi) is right that a catalog-unknown `deepseek-v4.1-flash` is treated as a plain model, so it requests no thinking and replays no `reasoning_content`:

```
400 The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API
```

That is a real consequence of hand-declaring the model. It is **not** a property of the model. `@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.87.1` ships the entry with the DeepSeek compat already attached. From `dist/providers/data/opencode-go.json`, under `openai-completions`:

"deepseek-v4.1-flash": {
  "api": "openai-completions",
  "baseUrl": "https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1",
  "reasoning": true,
  "compat": {
    "supportsStore": false,
    "supportsDeveloperRole": false,
    "supportsStrictMode": true,
    "maxTokensField": "max\_tokens",
    "requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages": true,
    "thinkingFormat": "deepseek"
  },
  "contextWindow": 1000000,
  "maxTokens": 384000
}

The two keys itchenshi identified as missing are present and identical to `deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` on the same route. On the catalog path there is nothing left to add — `reasoning_content` replay and `thinkingFormat` arrive with the entry.

### 2\. Coverage by path

Path

Session header

`reasoning_content` compat

Needs a DSH release

Dependency range widened

✅ pi-ai wrapper (`opencode-go.js:15-17`, all three protocols)

✅ carried by the catalog entry

yes

Jay0130-a adapter patch

✅ hand-derived, host-guarded

❌ catalog-unknown model still lacks it

no (if merged)

itchenshi plugin

✅

✅

no

The practical reading: itchenshi's point 3 is a correct objection **to the adapter patch**, not to the bump. If the goal is "make `deepseek-v4.1-flash` work on `opencode-go`", the bump is the only one of the three that clears both failures without new code in DSH.

### 3\. The two review points also apply upstream

Worth settling before maintainers pick a direction, because it affects the bump too. `dist/providers/opencode-headers.js` in 0.87.1 is:

function withSessionHeader(options) {
    if (!options?.sessionId || hasHeader(options.headers, OPENCODE\_SESSION\_HEADER))
        return options;
    return {
        ...options,
        headers: { ...options.headers, \[OPENCODE\_SESSION\_HEADER\]: options.sessionId },
    };
}

So (1) the value sent to OpenCode **is** the raw session id — the privacy concern is not specific to the patch; and (2) there is no character validation, so the CRLF-to-`TypeError` path exists there as well. Both are pi's design choices rather than DSH's, but "bump it and it's fixed" inherits them.

It does respect a pre-existing header (`hasHeader`), which is why a static `headers:` entry on a hand-declared route still wins — that is the workaround used in this thread, and it keeps working after a bump.

### 4\. Where the bump actually stands

Checked against published artifacts:

*   `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` declares `@earendil-works/pi-ai: ^0.85.1` in `0.1.5-rc.3`, `0.1.7-alpha.1`, `0.1.7-alpha.2`, and on `master` (`packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/package.json`).
*   `0.1.7-alpha.2` was published 2026-09-22 15:55 — **after** `0.87.0` (09-21 16:42) already existed. So this is not the release lagging the fix; the range simply has not been widened.
*   `0.87.1` is current on npm (09-22 19:38).

Under 0.x semver `^0.85.1` means `>=0.85.1 <0.86.0`, so 0.86.x and 0.87.x are both excluded — nothing between the installed catalog and the fix is reachable by upgrading DSH today.
